name: ui-layouts-carousel

frames.best_why: Frame 1 shows one slide fully framed with both arrows, the 1/4 counter and the dash dots.

tagline: A rounded photo slider with side arrows, a counter and dash dots.
summary: A horizontal image carousel with translucent round arrow buttons, a current-slide counter and dash-style dots. Slides glide sideways and wrap around at the ends.
appearance: A wide rounded photo slide, a white hillside town, with translucent circular arrow buttons at mid-left and mid-right. Below it a small mono counter reads 1 / 4 on the left and four short dash dots sit at the right.
behaviour: Clicking an arrow or dot slides the photo horizontally to the next frame with a short ease; the counter and the dark active dash update, and arrows dim at the ends. Arrow keys also page it.
demo_content: Santorini rooftops, a wooden deck and a seaside telescope
search_phrases: pictures that slide left and right
use_when: A page needs to show a handful of photos one at a time with simple controls.
avoid_when: Controls are fixed-size and the slide height is set in the demo, so tall art needs resizing.
customise: options and plugins drive the slider; slides, arrows, counter and dots are separate child components you compose and style.
weight_why: Four images with embla drag plus small counter animation; no canvas or loop.

a11y.note: Arrow buttons have no accessible names and the root hides its focus outline.

issues: Arrow buttons show only icons, with no labels for screen readers.
The slide counter is tiny mono text that is easy to miss.
polish_why: Clean rounded slider with tidy controls; default arrows and a tiny counter keep it standard.
